title: Composable customization strategy for customer Terraform overlays in VPC/private deployments
creator: Lena Rodriguez
description: Goal: define and prototype a composable, customer-friendly pattern for Terraform-based customizations used in Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. The pattern must support: tenant-specific overrides, environment overlays (dev/stage/prod), module composition for shared infra (networking, IAM, instance profiles), safe upgrade paths for platform changes, and automated health checks post-apply. This ticket captures recommended variable shapes, overlay layering, module boundaries, and a minimal reference implementation to ship to customers and Solutions Engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc describing three overlay strategies (overlay directories, wrapper modules, TF module composition) with pros/cons
Reference repository with working example: base module + two customer overlays + CI plan that runs terraform plan and a post-apply health check script
Upgrade procedure documented for breaking provider/module changes with an example of a state migration plan
Automation tests: linting (tflint), formatting (terraform fmt), and a Terraform plan guard that fails on drifts to disallowed changes
Runbook for Support/SE describing how to apply a customer overlay and roll back safely
implementation_notes: We recommend a hybrid approach: publish small, opinionated shared modules (network, kms, compute, routing) with a thin 'tenant-wrapper' module per customer that composes the shared modules and exposes only customer-tweakable variables. Overlays live in a second repo per-customer (private) or in a namespaced subdirectory: /overlays/{customer}/{env}. Use explicit variable objects to limit cross-surface changes: e.g., network = { vpc_id = string | null; subnets = list(string) } rather than separate scattered vars. For secrets use a provider-backed secret backend (S3 + KMS or Secrets Manager) rather than raw variables. Avoid relying on remote state manipulation by end-customers; provide a managed remote-state backend config helper.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge design doc and example repo to internal 'private-deploy-templates'. 2) Run an internal smoke deploy to staging customer account with overlay that changes CIDR and adds a sample service. 3) Collect feedback from Solutions Engineering. 4) Publish a customer-facing README and CI template. 5) Start onboarding two pilot customers and monitor for upgrade-edge cases.
comments: 2026-03-06 - Ravi Patel: Spiked three prototype layouts last week. The wrapper-module approach gave us the best guardrails but required tighter variable typing. Will update reference repo.

2026-03-10 - Lena Rodriguez: Added a draft of the state-migration section to Confluence. Need input from infra on whether we can support a 'schema' migration step in CI to migrate remote state when module outputs change names.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel: Implemented tflint and terraform-compliance in CI for the example repo. Plan guard rejects changes to cross-tenant network resources by default.
